description: DEMO CONFIG. Every block below is annotated so the repo doubles as documentation.
config:recommended    - Renovate's maintained baseline preset. Dependabot has no preset system at all.
:dependencyDashboard  - opens ONE tracking issue listing every pending/rate-limited/errored update,
with checkboxes that create the PR on demand. Dependabot has no equivalent.
group:monorepos       - auto-groups packages published from the same monorepo (e.g. @typescript-eslint/*)
from a community-maintained list. Zero per-package config.
Security fixes are raised PER PACKAGE so each one is independently mergeable -
a CVE fix should never be blocked by an unrelated package in the same branch.
The single exception is pip: requirements.txt pins exact versions with no lockfile,
so a partial bump leaves it unresolvable (flask 2.0.3 caps Jinja2<3.1, flask 3.1.3
requires Jinja2>=3.1.2). Python therefore moves as one coherent unit.
Weekly PR that regenerates package-lock.json from scratch, refreshing TRANSITIVE
dependencies that no manifest change would ever touch. Dependabot has no counterpart:
it only bumps transitives when an advisory names them.

customManagers.description: Update `ARG <TOOL>_VERSION=` lines in the Dockerfile using inline `# renovate:` annotations. No built-in manager - and no Dependabot feature - can do this.

packageRules.description: npm devDependencies, non-major. Grouped and automerged - the lockfile is regenerated per update, so a partial bump always resolves.
npm production, non-major. Separate from devDependencies because this one is reviewed.
Go, non-major. go.sum is regenerated per update so splitting is safe.
Docker base image, GitHub Actions and regex-managed tool versions, non-major.

Every major gets its OWN PR. Grouping majors is what made the previous devDependency-majors PR unmergeable: typescript 7 collided with the typescript-eslint peer range and took seven unrelated updates down with it. Isolated, soaked 21 days, held behind a dashboard checkbox.
ESCALATION - once the version in use is over 3 months old the checkbox gate lifts by itself, so nothing rots unnoticed in the queue.

npm devDependency majors: one PR each, automerged after a 30-day soak. Isolated rather than grouped so one unmergeable major cannot block the others. CI runs lint and typecheck, so a breaking eslint or typescript major fails the build instead of merging green.

Python is the one ecosystem that must NOT be split. requirements.txt pins exact versions and has no lockfile, so a partial bump leaves it unresolvable. groupName alone is not enough: separateMajorMinor defaults to true, which puts majors on their own branch under the same group name and reproduces the split. separateMajorMinor:false forces every pip update - major included - into one branch. Adopting pip-compile or uv would remove the need for this rule.

typescript is capped because @typescript-eslint/parser 8.x declares peer typescript ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0". Without the cap Renovate keeps raising a typescript 7 PR that can never pass npm ci. Suppressing an unresolvable update is better than shipping a permanently red PR. Remove when typescript-eslint supports v7.
prPriority only - runtime-critical packages surface first when the concurrent limit bites.
